unit.title: Present perfect subjunctive
unit.subtitle: haya hablado: subjunctive for completed actions

grammar.title: The subjunctive for things already done
grammar.intro: You already trigger the subjunctive after wishes, emotions, and doubt: me alegro de que…, espero que…, ojalá…. But what if the action is already completed? For that, Spanish uses the present perfect subjunctive: haya + past participle. So “I'm glad you came” becomes Me alegro de que hayas venido — the coming already happened, but the emotion still forces the subjunctive.

sections.heading: haya + past participle
sections.body: Take the subjunctive of haber and add the participle (the -ado / -ido form). It's the mirror of the normal perfect (he hablado → haya hablado):

ex.es: Me alegro de que hayas hablado con ella.
ex.en: I'm glad you've spoken with her.

sections.heading: When to use it
sections.body: Use it when a subjunctive trigger (emotion, hope, doubt) refers to something already finished. Compare present vs. perfect: Espero que llegue (I hope he arrives) vs. Espero que haya llegado (I hope he has arrived).

sections.heading: Irregular participles
sections.body: A handful of participles are irregular — the same ones as always. They pair with haya just like the regular ones:

ex.es: Me alegro de que hayas hecho la tarea.
ex.en: I'm glad you've done the homework.

ex.es: Es raro que no lo haya visto.
ex.en: It's strange that he hasn't seen it.

takeaways: Present perfect subjunctive = haya + past participle.
Forms: haya, hayas, haya, hayamos, hayáis, hayan.
Use it for completed actions in subjunctive contexts: Me alegro de que hayas venido.
Irregular participles stay irregular: hecho, visto, dicho, escrito, vuelto, puesto.

mistakes.w: Me alegro de que has venido.
mistakes.r: Me alegro de que hayas venido.
mistakes.why: After an emotion trigger, use the subjunctive haber: hayas, not has.

mistakes.w: Espero que haya llegado él ya. → Espero que has llegado.
mistakes.why: Keep the subjunctive form haya, not the indicative has, after 'espero que'.

mistakes.w: Me alegro de que hayas hacido la tarea.
mistakes.r: Me alegro de que hayas hecho la tarea.
mistakes.why: The participle of hacer is irregular: hecho, not hacido.
